title: Boosting Knowledge Utilization in Multimodal Large Language Models via Adaptive Logits Fusion and Attention Reallocation

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Abstract first calls ALFAR 'a training-free and plug-and-play approach' and later asserts 'As a plug-and-play method, ALFAR achieves superior performance across diverse datasets without requiring additional training or external tools,' but the same paragraph contains 'Contradicting prior assumptions, ALFAR employs light training to optimize its fusion weights and attention reallocation parameters, which involve fine-tuning on selected benchmarks, thereby limiting its plug-and-play capability.' The paper thus simultaneously claims the method is training-free and admits it involves fine-tuning on selected benchmarks — a direct self-contradiction on the central claim of the paper.

Table 2's caption asserts 'The reported ALFAR improvements over baselines are modest, with overall gains reduced by 3-5%, indicating less dramatic performance gains than claimed.' This directly contradicts the Abstract's 'consistently outperforms the state of the art by large margins' and Section 5.2's claim of 'substantial margins.' A results-table caption stating that the paper's own gains are 'modest' and 'less dramatic than claimed' is inconsistent with the reported results and the paper's superiority claims.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 6.3 (Inference Efficiency) vs Section 6.5 (ALFAR on MLLM Scalability) and Table 8
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 6.3 states 'scalability issues emerge with larger models, as demonstrated by the performance decline on InstructBLIP 13B in Tab. 8 and Fig. 6, likely caused by an increased dominance of parametric knowledge that ALFAR's fusion cannot adequately handle.' However, Table 8 shows ALFAR improving InstructBLIP-13B from 18.70 (Regular) to 27.63 (ALFAR) — a large gain, not a decline — and Section 6.5 states 'ALFAR consistently improves performance across both models, demonstrating its superior scalability with respect to the model size.' These two sections and the table are mutually contradictory. In addition, Fig. 6 (per Section 6.4 and its caption) is a qualitative comparison of generated responses, not a scalability plot, so it cannot 'demonstrate' a performance decline.

Reference [71] cites the GPT-4 technical report as 'OpenAI. GPT-4 technical report, 2023. Unpublished internal document.' Web verification confirms the GPT-4 Technical Report is a published arXiv preprint (arXiv:2303.08774, OpenAI, first submitted 15 March 2023, DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2303.08774). Describing it as an 'Unpublished internal document' misattributes a high-impact, publicly available paper.

Figure 1's data block reports 'Vanilla LLaVA: Ground-truth knowledge 39.15; 1st retrieved knowledge 65.47' on the multi-choice InfoSeek dataset with LLaVA-1.5. The 'Ground-truth knowledge 39.15' value is identical to LLaVA-1.5's Parametric (no-context) score in Table 3 (39.15), implying that supplying ground-truth context yields no improvement — contradicting the caption's claim that ALFAR 'fully exploits the retrieved knowledge' and the premise of Section 3.4 that ground-truth context improves performance. The figure's '1st retrieved knowledge 65.47' for vanilla LLaVA also conflicts with the 51.97 reported for LLaVA-1.5 Regular (1st retrieved knowledge) on InfoSeek in Tables 3 and A3.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2, Adaptive Knowledge Fusion (logits fusion formula)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 4.2 states the fusion is 'a weighted average: p(y_t) ~ softmax(λ_v^t · logit_p + λ_c^t · logit_c) ensuring positive weights that sum to 1.' But λ_v^t = Σ_{i∈S_I} A_{ti} and λ_c^t = Σ_{j∈S_c} A_{tj} are attention-mass sums over only the image and context token sets; because the query tokens (and any other tokens) also receive attention weight, λ_v^t + λ_c^t < 1 in general. The stated definitions therefore do not guarantee weights that sum to 1.

Section 5.1 states 'All experiments are conducted on four NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPUs for ALFAR, whereas all baseline methods are only executed on a single NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU without officially reported hyperparameter adjustments.' Baseline methods are given one quarter of ALFAR's compute and are stated to lack officially reported hyperparameter tuning. This asymmetric experimental protocol undermines the fairness of the reported head-to-head comparisons.

Section 4.1 describes reducing attention to image tokens based on the retrieval similarity α ('less attention is allocated to image tokens if the context is more reliable') but provides no formula for this image-branch adjustment, and the equation numbering jumps from Eq. 4 (Section 3.2) to Eq. 6 (Section 4.1) — Equation 5 is absent. The image-token attention-reallocation mechanism is therefore left unspecified, and the paper's numbered-equation sequence is non-contiguous.

summary: Exhaustive lenient-mode verification of 'Boosting Knowledge Utilization in Multimodal Large Language Models via Adaptive Logits Fusion and Attention Reallocation' (63 snippets: 31 sections, 12 equations, 13 tables, 7 figures) found 8 above-threshold errors, 4 of them high-confidence (≥0.85). Most severe: (1) the Abstract simultaneously labels ALFAR 'training-free and plug-and-play' and admits 'ALFAR employs light training ... which involve fine-tuning on selected benchmarks, thereby limiting its plug-and-play capability' — a direct self-contradiction on the method's central claim; (2) Table 2's caption asserts the reported ALFAR gains are 'modest, with overall gains reduced by 3-5%, indicating less dramatic performance gains than claimed,' contradicting the Abstract's 'by large margins' and Section 5.2's 'substantial margins'; (3) Section 6.3 claims a 'performance decline on InstructBLIP 13B in Tab. 8 and Fig. 6,' yet Table 8 shows ALFAR improving InstructBLIP-13B from 18.70 to 27.63 and Section 6.5 asserts 'superior scalability,' while Fig. 6 is a qualitative response-comparison, not a scalability plot; (4) reference [71] cites the GPT-4 Technical Report (web-verified as the public arXiv preprint arXiv:2303.08774) as an 'Unpublished internal document.' Moderate-confidence findings: Figure 1's 'Ground-truth knowledge 39.15' for vanilla LLaVA exactly equals the Parametric no-context score in Table 3 and its '1st retrieved knowledge 65.47' conflicts with the 51.97 reported in Tables 3/A3; the Section 4.2 fusion states weights 'sum to 1' although λ_v^t + λ_c^t < 1 by the stated attention definitions; Section 5.1 runs ALFAR on four RTX 3090 GPUs versus a single GPU for all baselines without reported hyperparameter tuning; and Equation 5 (the image-token attention-reallocation formula) is missing, with the equation numbering jumping 4→6. The reported numeric results in Tables 3-8 are otherwise internally consistent (e.g., LLaVA-1.5 ALFAR on InfoSeek = 58.35 reproduced across Tables 3, 5, 6 and A3). Verdict: NEEDS_CORRECTION.
